correctness.rationale: The unnormalized Fourier objective and support-inside convention are consistent, including N=5. For 3∤N, the quadratic with roots u,v is nonnegative at the sampled cosines and has strictly positive unscaled average 1/2+uv. The two positive dual multipliers force both zeros. Neither active level is ±1 (for even N≥8 there is a sample strictly between 2π/3 and π, and a positive-angle sample below 2π/3 for every N≥5). Nonnegativity at both signed frequencies then forces the two odd coefficients to vanish. For 3|N, the opposite third-root samples force a+b=1 and equal imaginary coefficients at the optimum. The factorization reduces the constraints to b≥L+|t|cot(θ_u/2) and b≤R−|t|cot(θ_v/2): that pair first forces |t|≤T, so monotone selection of the upper bound is only needed on that feasible interval. At b=B,t=T the relevant second-factor numerators become 1+2cos(θ∓β), vanishing at θ_u,θ_v respectively. For N≥9, β<0.7 gives T≤0.7/(3−0.7²)<1/(2√3); hence all other bounds are weaker. At N=6 only the adjacent samples matter and L=B, making (L,0) nonextreme. A separate floating-point enumeration of active quadruples in the full four-real-coordinate feasible polytope found exactly the predicted optimal vertices for N=5 through 24, including 3 vertices at 6 and 4 at 9,12,15,18,21,24. Replay: python3 /workspace/reproductions/frozen_checks.py 1. Neither this bounded numerical check nor the frozen checker is used as an all-N proof; the frozen checker does not directly enumerate the full nonresonant complex face.
